key_decisions.decision: Render the toledot heading consistently as a family record and preserve the repeated Esau/Edom identification.
Make the two generations in Oholibamah’s ancestry explicit while preserving the wife names and peoples and leaving their differences from earlier wife lists visible.
Follow the recorded reading Jeush in the exact source record, preserve every name and birthplace, and flag the written/read form in a note.
Repeat the toledot heading naturally and render father as ancestor of the people while retaining Edom and Seir.
Make the ancestry levels explicit, preserve all sons, and follow the source record’s traditional reading Jeush without concealing its written form.
Use chief consistently for alluf, keep Esau and Eliphaz’s firstborn relationship, and begin the continuous clan-leader list.
Retain the source’s placement of Korah in Eliphaz’s list despite the tension with verse 14 and keep the land and maternal line.
Retain the two sons, wilderness setting, work, and father while choosing hot springs for the uncertain yemim and disclosing alternatives.
Retain the narrator’s comparative time marker and political language without inserting a theory about composition or fulfillment.
Keep the exact king, father, military action, peoples, territory, and city without celebrating the violence.
Preserve the source’s Hadar reading, city, and unusually detailed female genealogy while clarifying the broad daughter term as a second generation.
Complete the chief list and preserve settlements, possessed land, and the final Esau/Edom identification without replacing the concrete father language.
